name: q2_holder_cold_asked
question: Q2 (faded register)
what_it_tests: A COLD holder asked straight. Warin Bluehand heard about the turned Brede cart a long while back and it has cooled off his sheet's warm half; relevance has seated it anyway, in the faded register. Does he answer with the vagueness the hedge gives him instead of either sharpening it into detail or claiming ignorance he does not have? He also carries a second fact whose subject he does NOT know, which is where unknown_person.txt is exercised.

what_you_know.said: a Brede cart was turned at the Wool Gate; the beam called it forty pounds over
{subject} promised a weaver's bolt a place on the Brede cart, and took a penny for the word

sheet.you: Warin Bluehand, 37, male — Dyer (Cloth worker, master) of The Cut. Home: a house in the Weigh Ward, off the Cut. Family: mother Nan (id e9nan); children: Cobb (id e3cob).
sheet.back_story: Blue to the elbow and not sorry for it, you keep a small woad-and-madder dye-house on the Cut: thirty-seven, a master by your own clawing, journeyman to master out of pure spite after Ewart Skell had you put out of the cloth hall like a dog that fouled the floor. You are loud, quick, coarse and funny about your own life; you shout the length of a lane, you say the name Skell the way a man spits a pip, and you hold up your stained hands to strangers as if they were a guild seal. Every quarter you send money to your son Cobb on Tenterhook Lane and every quarter it comes back untouched, and you send it again, because to stop would be to agree with him. You want the Reach to weigh your blues honestly and call you master to your face; you are afraid of dying with a boy in this city who will not say your name over you. Your mother Nan still washes cloth on the Cut at sixty-six and tells you plainly that spite is a poor dye and never holds, and you love her, and you do not listen.
sheet.you_are: On the Cut, walking down toward the Tally Bridge (x -214, z 314).

sheet.current_goal: Get the bolt to the Draper's Reach before the rain
